Subject: RE: Follow-up + next steps after today's call — tech note (SDK/auth + retries)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Per Lauren's recap, below is a concise set of recommendations and examples you can use during the PoC. I focused on SDK initialization, auth patterns, routing fallbacks, and a robust retry/idempotency strategy for 429 handling.

1) SDK & Auth (server-side calls)- Use our server SDK with a short-lived service token. Recommended pattern:
  - Exchange your long-lived service key for a short-lived session token via our control-plane endpoint from a secure backend.
  - Initialize SDK with session token and enable automatic refresh (sample init in api-examples.txt).

2) Routing & Model variants- Configure a routing policy that prefers your dedicated model pool (low-latency). Fallback policy:
  - If the dedicated pool returns 429 or explicit "capacity_exceeded", route to a compatible hosted variant (same architecture, slightly lower throughput).
  - Maintain request header X-Redwood-Routing: preferred=dedicated;fallback=hosted.

3) Rate limits & quotas (starter profile for PoC)- Based on the traffic you shared, start with:
  - Token quota: 5M tokens/day (adjust after PoC).
  - Burst / concurrency: 3k concurrent tokens/minute; request concurrency cap: 250 concurrent requests.
  - We'll monitor and recommend tuned settings during PoC ramp.

4) Retry strategy (429 + 5xx) and idempotency- Goals: avoid thundering herd, provide predictable client behavior, and dedupe side-effecting operations.
  a) Idempotency keys: require an Idempotency-Key header for any write-style endpoint (create/commit/export). Use a UUIDv4 per logical operation. Store mapping on your side for retries.
  b) Retry logic for safe (read) calls like generation/embeddings/rerank: use exponential backoff with full jitter: base=200ms, factor=2, max=10s, cap retries=5.
  c) For 429 responses: 
    - Honor Retry-After header if present (use server-provided seconds).
    - If Retry-After absent, apply exponential backoff with jitter as above.
    - When receiving repeated 429s from dedicated pool, attempt single immediate fallback to hosted variant once (to avoid double-issuing).
  d) For non-idempotent write endpoints:
    - Reject automatic client retries unless user supplies Idempotency-Key. Server will return 409 if the same key was previously used with a different payload.

5) Embeddings + reranking pattern- Batch embeddings server-side in small groups (8–32) to improve throughput and lower per-unit cost; keep request sizes under 1k tokens for best latency. For real-time UI flows, consider async fetch + cached prefixes to avoid blocking UI.

6) Observability hooks- Add X-Request-Id for tracing and include X-Redwood-Model and X-Redwood-Region. Send sample logs to us for quick tuning.

Attachments: architecture-diagram.png (high-level flow), api-examples.txt (init/auth snippets), poc-scope.pdf

I'll follow with a short PoC checklist in a separate message. Happy to jump on a technical kickoff.

Cheers,
Connor O'Brien
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: api-examples.txt]

Subject: Re: Follow-up + next steps after today's call — PoC checklist + answers

Alex / Priya — quick follow-up to answer Priya's questions and to summarize next steps.

On retention for Idempotency-Key mappings: Redwoods stores idempotency mappings for 7 days by default for Dedicated customers; for hosted-only we retain 24 hours but can extend via contract for your PoC period.

Per-minute token buckets: yes — we recommend a token bucket per API key tied to the quota profile. For the PoC start: allocate 50k tokens/min per API key with an account-level cap at 3k concurrent tokens/min (as Connor noted).

If hosted fallback is saturated during peak we recommend the following escalation order:
 1) Client auto-throttle + queue short-term (10–30s) to absorb spikes.
 2) If sustained beyond 2–5 minutes, trigger autoscale to allocate extra Dedicated capacity (we can enable burst capacity for your account).
 3) Redwood CS/SE will be alerted via our SRE runbook and will coordinate.

Proposed PoC checklist (attached poc-scope.pdf):
- Share anonymized search logs (Atlas) — due Tue May 5.
- Redwood to provision PoC dedicated pool (small) and initial quota profile — Redwood (Lauren/Connor) by Wed May 6.
- Technical kickoff (30m) — target week of May 10.
- Deliverables: sample SDK init & auth snippet, retry/idempotency guidance (this thread), architecture diagram, PoC success criteria.

I'll attach the architecture diagram and the PoC scope. Connor / Rishi will be on the kickoff. If this schedule works, I will send calendar invites.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
